blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 1
A DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF APOSTATES PART 1
Scripture Text: Jude 12

In the last quarterly, we learned that the Epistle of Jude is a gateway to The Revelation because it introduces us to highly symbolic language. The tone of verse 12 is almost totally symbolic. Jude called apostates spots, clouds, and trees. These figurative expressions were used to bring certain images to our minds so that Jude could convey the truth concerning the description of apostates.
MEMORY VERSE: That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish (Ephesians 5:27).
Spots Among God’s People

These are spots in your feasts of charity . . . feeding themselves without fear. These words are referring to people spoken of in the previous verses. In the original Greek, the word used for spots is spilas. It means “a half-submerged rock on which a ship could be easily shipwrecked.” This teaches us that associating with apostates could cause us to make a spiritual shipwreck of our faith (see 1 Timothy 1:19).

In the morning time, apostates used the feasts of charity to influence others. There may be times, such as at weddings or funerals, when you will meet ones who will be feeding themselves without fear. Another translation of this phrase is, “They have no feelings of responsibility for anyone except themselves.” Be careful! Although apostates are friendly, they are deadly. They are feeding themselves without fear only “because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily . . .” (Ecclesiastes 8:11).
Clouds and Winds

Clouds they are without water, carried about of winds. Proverbs 25:14 says, “Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift is like clouds and wind without rain.” Apostates boast of gifts and callings that they do not have. Their professions are as false and empty as clouds with no water. The words without water come from the same Greek word that is translated “dry places” in Matthew 12:43. “Dry places” are where unclean spirits wander. People who are in an apostate condition are there because they gave heed to unclean spirits. In turn, these spirits have given them false gifts.

The next part of our text are the words carried about of winds. Ephesians 4:14 speaks of being “carried about with every wind of doctrine.” When ones come under the power of unclean spirits, they are led to believe in “doctrines of devils” (1 Timothy 4:1). Seducing spirits cause people to be carried about, or be moved from one position to another. Their spirit changes and they alter their beliefs.
The Spiritual Trees

Trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit. These trees are people who, spiritually speaking, were once good trees. They once produced good spiritual fruit, according to Matthew 7:17. Unfortunately, their fruit died. Now, they are without fruit. What type of fruit was Jude speaking of? Romans 6:22 says, “But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness . . . .” When one’s spirit changes from the Holy Spirit to an unclean spirit, he is committing iniquity, and “all his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned” (Ezekiel 18:24). Why? His fruit of holiness has withered; and when a spiritual tree is without the fruit of holiness, it is known as having died twice.

SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 1
A Tragic Condition

Twice dead. The term twice dead sounds strange. It describes those who were once spiritually dead in their sins, then they were saved by being “born of the Spirit” (John 3:8); but tragically, they died spiritually, again. The sad thing about the condition of being twice dead is that it can be final and irreversible.

What could possibly make this condition so hopeless? The fact that God cannot renew someone’s experience while that one still professes to be saved. One who is spiritually dead must first acknowledge his condition, then he can be made alive. When David was confronted with his sin by the Prophet Nathan, he acknowledged his sin (Psalm 51:3). When old Israel was in apostasy, she said, “I am innocent . . . I have not sinned” (Jeremiah 2:35). There is no help for ones who will not admit their condition! They are, as Proverbs 30:12 declares, “pure in their own eyes, and yet . . . not washed from their filthiness.”
The Horrible Deception

Plucked up by the roots. This description shows the sad permanence of the condition of one overtaken by the spirit of apostasy. Jesus described this condition in Matthew 15:13: “Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.” What causes these plants to be “rooted up”? The answer is found in Matthew 15:12. Jesus’ disciples came to Him and asked, “Knowest thou that the Pharisees were offended, after they heard this saying?” The religious Pharisees were offended at Jesus’ Word!

When ones become offended and begin to profess and will not take the Word, that same Word will cause them to be “rooted up.” Study the Scriptures; you will see that this is the historical record. (Read Deuteronomy 29:28, 1 Kings 14:15, Psalm 52:5, Proverbs 2:22, and Jeremiah 1:10.)

The words plucked up imply a deliberate action. They reveal the fact that when people persist so far in their folly, God Himself will take action. He will send them a man with a message. If that Word is rejected, it will root out, or pull up, the ones who are offended by it, and they will leave. 2 Thessalonians 2:11-12 says: “And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.”

What is the “lie” that apostates believe? They believe that their unrighteousness is truth. This is why they are “damned” and cannot get any help. They continue to think they still have the truth! May God help us to keep our hearts “with all diligence” (Proverbs 4:23), for we are not immune to the power of this spirit.
JUST A THOUGHT
Truth is not truth because honest men consent to it, but honest men will consent to truth because it is truth.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 2
A DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF APOSTATES PART 2
Scripture Text: Jude 13

In the last lesson, Jude used words from nature to portray apostasy: clouds, winds, trees, and roots. In this lesson, he continues to use symbolic language: raging waves of the sea and wandering stars. These descriptive words are called metaphors.

As we study verse 13, we must remember that it is a continuation of the sentence that began in verse 12. The metaphors raging waves and wandering stars are only continued descriptions of the people meant by the word these in verse 12. Each of these metaphors has two common aspects: instability and action. The people represented by these symbols are active–constantly working to affect others.
MEMORY VERSE: Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness (1 Thessalonians 5:5).
Who Are the Wicked?

Raging waves of the sea. Who in the Scriptures are represented as being raging waves of the sea? Isaiah 57:20 says, “The wicked are like the troubled sea.” This verse equates the sea with the “wicked.” Psalm 50:16-17 says: “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth? Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” In God‟s sight, the “wicked” are those who do not take His instruction or regard His Word, yet they profess to be His followers. They are religious professors–ones who are teachers, preachers, and advocates of religion. Our lesson text calls these ones raging waves of the sea.

This is the picture Jude was portraying: these raging waves of the sea (ones overtaken by apostasy) would like to beat against the church with much fierceness and rage, hoping to move it from its position and submerge it from public view. In the morning-time apostasy, the church was hidden from public view for a time.

However, waves cannot maintain their positions permanently. Psalm 104:9 declares, “Thou hast set a bound that they may not pass over.” Psalm 89:9 states, “Thou rulest the raging of the sea: when the waves thereof arise, thou stillest them.” The saint who has a clear vision of truth knows that apostates, in their assault upon the truth, will do just what a wave hitting a rock does: it becomes foam–and those who attack the church only foam out their shame.
Great Swelling Words

Foaming out their own shame. Zephaniah 3:5 says, “The unjust knoweth no shame.” Philippians 3:19 says that their “glory is in their shame.” In other words, as one translation says, “They are proud of what they should be ashamed of.” The Greek word that is translated shame in Jude 13 is translated dishonesty in 2 Corinthians 4:2. Ones who are in the condition of apostasy are there because they became dishonest, and their actions are foaming out their own shame. Those with honest and good hearts, “having heard the word, keep it” (Luke 8:15). They stay in the truth.

Notice the word foaming. It comes from the Greek word epaphrizo, which means “to foam upon, to exhibit a vile passion, to foam out.” Apostates exhibit their vileness and dishonesty by speaking against the way of truth. 2 Peter 2:18 says, “For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error.”

LESSON 2

The Apostle Peter was actually saying that when assaults by apostates do not accomplish what they intend, then they will resort to flattery. They will appeal to people‟s vanity. 2 Peter 2:19 says that they promise ones “liberty”; but all they really have to offer is “corruption” and “bondage.” These people are constantly shifting their positions as waves do. (Remember, Jude 12 said they were “plucked up by the roots.”) They no longer have a connection to the truth. They are unstable, and all they can do is work to deceive other unstable souls.
A Misguided Ministry

Wandering stars. This phrase is a very disturbing metaphor. It explains why so many people are spiritually off course. In the natural realm, stars are unchanging in their positions. A seaman can chart transoceanic courses and navigate by their predetermined locations. But these are wandering stars: ones that follow uncertain courses.

In the Bible, what do stars represent? Revelation 1:20 says, “The seven stars are the angels [the Greek word is aggelos; it means „messengers‟ or „ministers‟] of the seven churches.” Stars represent the ministry. In Matthew 2:9, the “star” led the wise men to Christ and to the house in which He resided. Ministers are to lead men to Christ and to the house where He resides: the church. Wandering stars are a ministry whose position, or course, continues to change. Is it any wonder that the people who sit under such a ministry are confused?

Proverbs 21:16 states, “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.” Wandering stars have gotten “out of the way of understanding.” They had light, but they failed to walk in it while they had it. Apostate ministers, in essence, are spiritually blind. Jesus said, “If the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch” (Matthew 15:14). While these wandering stars profess to be the true ministry, they have, in reality, deceived themselves and are misleading people.
A Great Darkness

To whom is reserved the blackness of darkness forever. Part of this phrase sounds repetitious: the blackness of darkness. But notice the phrase before it: to whom is reserved. The Greek word for reserved is tereo. It means “to keep or detain as in custody.” Something is keeping these wandering stars, or ministers, in this condition. These people are kept, or held, by the blackness of darkness. They are in darkness and are captives of a blackness of their own making.

The reason the darkness is so black is that they have walked away from light and “put darkness for light, and light for darkness” (Isaiah 5:20). Matthew 6:23 says, “If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!” Only light can bring them deliverance, but when ones believe that light is darkness and darkness is light, they are in an irreversible position as long as they hold to that way of thinking.
JUST A THOUGHT
Light is the most glorious thing if you walk in it; it is the most blinding thing if you do not!

Psalm 50:16-17 says: “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?
Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.”
In God‟s sight, the “wicked” are those who do not take His instruction or regard His Word, yet they profess to be His followers.
They are religious professors–ones who are teachers, preachers, and advocates of religion.
Our lesson text calls these ones raging waves of the sea.

This is the picture Jude was portraying: these raging waves of the sea (ones overtaken by apostasy) would like to beat against the church with much fierceness and rage, hoping to move it from its position and submerge it from public view.
In the morning-time apostasy, the church was hidden from public view for a time.
However, waves cannot maintain their positions permanently.
Psalm 104:9 declares, “Thou hast set a bound that they may not pass over.”
Psalm 89:9 states, “Thou rulest the raging of the sea: when the waves thereof arise, thou stillest them.”

The saint who has a clear vision of truth knows that apostates, in their assault upon the truth, will do just what a wave hitting a rock does: it becomes foam–and those who attack the church only foam out their shame.
Foaming out their own shame.
Zephaniah 3:5 says, “The unjust knoweth no shame.”
Philippians 3:19 says that their “glory is in their shame.”
In other words, as one translation says, “They are proud of what they should be ashamed of.”
The Greek word that is translated shame in Jude 13 is translated dishonesty in 2 Corinthians 4:2.
Ones who are in the condition of apostasy are there because they became dishonest, and their actions are foaming out their own shame.
Those with honest and good hearts, “having heard the word, keep it” (Luke 8:15).
They stay in the truth.
Notice the word foaming.
It comes from the Greek word epaphrizo, which means “to foam upon, to exhibit a vile passion, to foam out.”
Apostates exhibit their vileness and dishonesty by speaking against the way of truth.

2 Peter 2:18 says, “For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error.”
The Apostle Peter was actually saying that when assaults by apostates do not accomplish what they intend, then they will resort to flattery.
They will appeal to people‟s vanity.
2 Peter 2:19 says that they promise ones “liberty”; but all they really have to offer is “corruption” and “bondage.”
These people are constantly shifting their positions as waves do. (Remember, Jude 12 said they were “plucked up by the roots.”) They no longer have a connection to the truth.
They are unstable, and all they can do is work to deceive other unstable souls.
Wandering stars.
This phrase is a very disturbing metaphor.
It explains why so many people are spiritually off course.
In the natural realm, stars are unchanging in their positions.
A seaman can chart transoceanic courses and navigate by their predetermined locations.
But these are wandering stars: ones that follow uncertain courses.
In the Bible, what do stars represent?
Revelation 1:20 says, “The seven stars are the angels [the Greek word is aggelos; it means „messengers‟ or „ministers‟] of the seven churches.”
Stars represent the ministry.
In Matthew 2:9, the “star” led the wise men to Christ and to the house in which He resided.
Ministers are to lead men to Christ and to the house where He resides: the church.
Wandering stars are a ministry whose position, or course, continues to change.
Is it any wonder that the people who sit under such a ministry are confused?
Proverbs 21:16 states, “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.”
Wandering stars have gotten “out of the way of understanding.”
They had light, but they failed to walk in it while they had it.
Apostate ministers, in essence, are spiritually blind.
Jesus said, “If the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch” (Matthew 15:14).
While these wandering stars profess to be the true ministry, they have, in reality, deceived themselves and are misleading people.
To whom is reserved the blackness of darkness forever.
Part of this phrase sounds repetitious: the blackness of darkness.
But notice the phrase before it: to whom is reserved.
The Greek word for reserved is tereo.
It means “to keep or detain as in custody.”
Something is keeping these wandering stars, or ministers, in this condition.
These people are kept, or held, by the blackness of darkness.
They are in darkness and are captives of a blackness of their own making.
The reason the darkness is so black is that they have walked away from light and “put darkness for light, and light for darkness” (Isaiah 5:20).
Matthew 6:23 says, “If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!”
Only light can bring them deliverance, but when ones believe that light is darkness and darkness is light, they are in an irreversible position as long as they hold to that way of thinking.
Light is the most glorious thing if you walk in it; it is the most blinding thing if you do not!

lessons.title: A DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF APOSTATES PART 2

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 3
ENOCH THE PROPHET
Scripture Text: Jude 14

In this verse, Jude went back into the Book of Genesis to illustrate truth in his day. This time he used Enoch . . . the seventh from Adam. He told us that Enoch was a prophet (this is the only Scriptural account of this fact), and he equated his prophesy with the judgments that apostates will receive.

MEMORY VERSE: By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God (Hebrews 11:5).
A Biblical Type

Enoch also, the seventh from Adam. This phrase shows that Jude was careful to identify whom he was speaking of because there was another Enoch: the son of Cain, the murderer. The Hebrew name Enoch means, “dedicated, disciplined, and well regulated,” which shows that if an individual wants to walk with God, he must be dedicated to Him. The Holy Spirit must be allowed to discipline and direct his life.

What significance does the expression the seventh from Adam hold? When we think of Adam, we immediately think of the fall of man, of sin, and of death. Romans 5:12 says, “By one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin.” Romans 5:14 declares that “death reigned from Adam to Moses.” 1 Corinthians 10:11 states that “all these things happened unto them for [our] ensamples,” or as one translation says, “by way of type.”

Webster’s New World Dictionary defines the word type as “a person, a thing, or an event that represents or symbolizes another, especially another that is to come.” What is the lesson in this type? Seven, biblically, denotes perfection and completeness. Beginning with Adam, six generations were subject to sin and death, but with the seventh from Adam something happened. Enoch, who was perfect, “was translated that he should not see death” (Hebrews 11:5). He was taken out of this world never again to be exposed to sin and death. He is now enjoying irrevocable eternal life.

So it is in this Gospel dispensation. Men have been exposed to sin and death from the first period of time, but at the end of the seventh and last period of time, those who are perfect, those who have walked with God, will be taken at the Lord’s coming and will be forever removed from the power of sin and death to enjoy eternal life.
The Prophecy of Enoch

Prophesied of these. Some have difficulty with the fact that Jude quoted from a book that is not recorded as part of the accepted Scriptures. (The quote in verse 15 is from Enoch 1:9.) Remember, “holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost” (2 Peter 1:21). Often they spoke from writings that their audience was familiar with. (Paul quoted Grecian poets to the Greeks on Mars’ Hill.)Because a writing is not found within the Scriptures does not mean that it has no merit. Many truths were derived from other writings. The fact that they were quoted in the New Testament is proof that they were authentic. What is incorporated there is just the amount that the Lord wanted to be in the Scriptures.

Consider the prophecy of Enoch. Genesis 5:21 says that he begat Methuselah. Methuselah lived to be the oldest man in the Bible, living 969 years (Genesis 5:27). His long life is a type that represents the Lord’s longsuffering with man. God is “not willing that any should perish” (2 Peter 3:9). The name Methuselah literally means, “When he is dead, it shall be sent.” In giving this name to his son, Enoch was prophesying. He knew of the coming Flood and God’s judgment upon the people living then. Therefore, Jude cited Enoch as he spoke of the fate of apostates to let them know that their fate would be very similar to those people.

SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 3
Are You Ready for Eternity?

Behold, the Lord cometh. What is the message in these words? Concerning apostasy, Jude was trying to emphasize that we should live with the thought of the Lord’s coming on our minds at all times. If those who have been making a profession of religion really had eternity on their minds, they would be living much differently.

There is more than just this time world to consider. One day time will be no more. That which we believe, teach, and live must be able to withstand the shock of Judgment Day. 2 Corinthians 5:10 says, “We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ.” We need to make our decisions and moves carefully and prayerfully, based on the fact that the Lord cometh! If we will do this, then everything will take on a more serious purpose. To avoid the ultimate end of apostasy, we need to be living and walking according to truth so that we can say, “Even so, come, Lord Jesus” (Revelation 22:20).
JUST A THOUGHT
If you will live as you ought, with the Judgment in view, you will not need to review what you do!

LESSON 4
THE LORD COMETH WITH TEN THOUSANDS OF HIS SAINTS
Scripture Text: Jude 14
The last lesson concluded with a study of the phrase behold, the Lord cometh. In this lesson we want to consider it a little more, along with the remaining phrase: with ten thousands of his saints.

In the world, Christians often feel that they are few. However, this prophecy reveals that there are many who have been God’s saints. On the Judgment Day, those who have already stepped from this life will return with the Lord.
MEMORY VERSE: Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment: because as he is, so are we in this world (1 John 4:17).
The Lord’s Return

Behold, the Lord cometh. As we learned previously, the Prophet Enoch declared that the Lord would come in the last days. We are still waiting for this event. However, we are living in the last days, and 2 Peter 3:3-4 declares that in the last days scoffers will come asking, “Where is the promise of his coming?” The coming of the Lord is an established biblical fact. Jesus spoke of it in His final words in Matthew, Chapters 24, 25, and 26. Many other Scriptures tell of Christ’s coming as well, so even in the face of modern skepticism, we can see that this is a clear biblical teaching.
The Countless Multitude

With ten thousands. Why is this particular phrase used? Revelation 7:9 tells us that the saints are a great, numberless multitude. In Genesis 15:5 God said to Abraham, “Look now toward heaven, and tell [or try to count] the stars, if thou be able to number them . . . So shall thy seed be.” Genesis 32:12 says, “I will . . . make thy seed as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.”

Why is a numerical expression used in the lesson text when the number of the saints is without number? The words used in the English text are ten thousands. In Greek this number is not meant to be taken literally. It is an expression. The actual Greek word that was used, murias, means “a myriad, an innumerable amount.” The Emphatic Diaglott translates the phrase ten thousands as “with his Holy Myriads.”

John described those around the throne in Revelation 5:11 by saying, “The number of them, was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands.” This phrase in The Emphatic Diaglott reads, “The number of them was Myriads of Myriads, and Thousands of Thousands.” The word myriads means “an immense number: an indefinitely large number.” In English, if we wanted to express an innumerable amount, we would say millions and millions. Since there is no Greek word for millions, it is expressed as myriads or ten thousands.
Saints Will Be Avenged

His saints. When Jesus comes again, He will come with all the departed saints–He will not be alone. Jude brought up this fact when he was dealing with apostasy because apostates always claim that the saints are wrong. The Judgment Day will reveal who really is with the Lord. Those who have gone to their graves slandered by heretics and apostates will be vindicated, or avenged, on that day. Their very appearance with the Lord will serve as an eternal confirmation of the truth for which they stood. The notable absence of any

LESSON 4
apostates in the ranks of God’s people will serve as the final denunciation of their apostate preaching and practices.

The sad fact is, many apostates will do as Jesus said they would in Matthew 7:22-23. They will say: “Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name have done many wonderful works?”

To be apostates, ones had to have known truth. To have “cast out devils,” they could not have been of Satan at that time. Matthew 12:26 tells us why: “And if Satan cast out Satan . . . how shall then his kingdom stand?” But Jesus said in Matthew 7:23, “I never knew you. Depart from me, ye that work iniquity.” Ezekiel 28:15 says, “Thou wast perfect . . . till iniquity was found in thee.”

When men do wrong, they are no longer in a state of perfection. Ezekiel 18:24 says, “But when the righteous turneth away from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity . . . shall he live? [No.] All his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned.” This is why Jesus will say to ones, “I never knew you.” Jude was teaching all who would take heed that there is coming a day that will expose everything and strike terror into the hearts of all who are wrong.
The Body Reaps Its Reward

There is another reason the Lord will come with all the deceased saints. When physical death happens to a saved individual, the soul–the eternal part of man–goes to be with Christ. The physical part–the body–is buried, or sown, as a seed and sleeps in Jesus (see 1 Thessalonians 4:14). (The unsaved soul goes to hell to await judgment, according to Revelation 20:13.)

On Judgment Day, the deceased saints will return with Christ to have their souls and bodies reunited. 1 Corinthians 15:52-53 states: “The dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed. For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.” These verses refer to just the body; nothing has been said about the soul regarding the Resurrection, because Christ will be bringing the saved souls with Him.

Why will the soul be reunited with the body? Because the body is the instrument of the soul in life. It, too, must reap the reward for its deeds. 2 Corinthians 5:10 states, “For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.” When the body comes forth from the grave on Judgment Day, it will be made immortal. After being reunited with the soul, the body will receive judgment, not for its fate, but for the degree of its deeds. Together, they will be dispatched for eternity.

Jude brought up this serious thought so that those who have been influenced by apostasy to live loosely might consider what their final end could be. Since all bodies and souls will be reunited to reap their eternal rewards, shouldn’t we stop and think before we embrace wrong thinking? Ephesians 5:15 says, “Walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise.”
JUST A THOUGHT
You should live with the Judgment in view; for one day, the Judgment shall view you!

LESSON 5
THE JUDGMENT OF APOSTATES
Scripture Text: Jude 15

Jude 15 pertains to the Judgment. In the lesson text, Jude is still quoting the Prophet Enoch. The fact that Enoch had such clear insight about the final judgment shows that this is a truth of such importance to God that He wanted all of human history to have an awareness of it.
MEMORY VERSE: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil (Ecclesiastes 12:14).
Judgment for All

To execute judgment upon all. When the Lord comes, He will come as a judge. 2 Timothy 4:1 says, “I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick [those alive] and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom.” Christ will judge both saint and sinner. “For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ” (Romans 14:10). Matthew 25:32 states that all nations shall be gathered before Christ. In others words, all mankind–alive or dead–will be there on that day.

Some teachers of religion try to use part of 2 Peter 2:9 (“to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished”) and part of 2 Peter 3:7 (“the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men”) to teach that only the “unjust” and “ungodly” will ever come into judgment. One writer has said that the Greek word for judgment in our text, krisis, is never used in regards to believers, but this is not so. 1 John 4:17 tells us, “Herein is our love made perfect, that we [the saints] may have boldness in the Day of Judgment.” The same Greek word, krisis, is used here just as it is in 2 Peter.
Are You Ungodly?

To convince all that are ungodly . . . of all their ungodly deeds . . . they have ungodly committed, and ... ungodly sinners. In verse 15 the word ungodly is used four times. It is used to refer to the condition of the people: all that are ungodly. It is used to describe what they have done: ungodly deeds . . . ungodly committed. Finally, it is used to describe their spiritual state: ungodly sinners. What do all these descriptions tell us? They tell us that the spiritual condition of a person’s heart dictates his deeds. LESSON 5
Degree of Destiny

To execute judgment upon . . . their ungodly deeds. Look now at the criterion, or basis, for judgment. Man’s judgment will not be based on the state of his soul or his spiritual condition. That has already been determined. How do we know? Remember, Jude 14 said “Behold, the Lord cometh with . . . his saints,” and this verse says “To execute judgment.” So, it is obvious that before the beginning of the final Judgment, the saints will already be known as such.

Prior to the Judgment, the final state of all deceased souls was determined at death. Luke 16:19-31 shows us that before the Resurrection and the Judgment, the rich man went to hell, and Lazarus went to “Abraham’s bosom.” Jesus told the repentant thief, in Luke 23:43 that he would be with Him in paradise. When one dies, the state of the soul is immediately sealed. It is either saved or lost (see Ecclesiastes 11:3). A man’s eternal destiny is determined by the state of his soul at his death or at the Second Coming, whichever one comes first. The final Judgment only determines the degree of his destiny based on his deeds.

The reason final judgment does not occur immediately after death is that the influence and works of our lives live on until time stops. We cannot be given a proper reckoning until then. (Jude has been dead for around twenty centuries, but his works are still benefitting us as recently as today.) We will be judged according to the deeds we have done. This is verified throughout the Scriptures (Psalm 62:12, Ecclesiastes 12:14, Matthew 16:27, Romans 2:6, and 1 Peter 1:17).

The degrees of reward or punishment will be based on a person’s knowledge, his deeds, and his actions. Matthew 23:14 speaks of “greater damnation.” Hebrews 10:29 mentions “sorer punishment.” Luke 12:47-48 tells of “many stripes” for some and “few stripes” for others. Since Christ will pass sentence on us based on our deeds, we ought to give serious consideration to whatever we do and say. Revelation 22:12 states, “And behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.”
JUST A THOUGHT
A deed might seem small to the doer, but it could have a big impact on the recipient.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 6
THE PROGRESSIVE NATURE OF APOSTASY
Scripture Text: Jude 16

In verses 14 and 15, Jude’s thoughts reverted to the oldest of the Old Testament prophets, Enoch. In verse 16, however, he returned to those whom he had been exposing–the apostates in the first century–and proved that, from the first century to the twenty-first century, the nature of apostasy has never changed. It is a progressive nature. Webster’s New World Dictionary defines the word progressive as “moving forward or onward, continuing by successive steps.”

MEMORY VERSE: Do all things without murmurings and disputings: That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world (Philippians 2:14-15).
The Gradual Progression

These are murmurers. Apostasy is a condition that only continues to worsen. Psalm 1:1 shows its progressive nature: “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.”

1 Corinthians 9:24 equates the Christian life to a race. Notice, Psalm 1:1 says, “walketh,” “standeth,” and “sitteth.” These words show a gradual decline and change of pace. If you are one who is listening to the “counsel of the ungodly,” you will gradually slow down in your race from a run to a walk, but you will not stop there. Soon, you will be one who stands “in the way of sinners.” Once the seeds of apostasy have been sown in your mind, “. . . ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in” (Matthew 23:13). Finally, you will be one who sits “in the seat of the scornful.”

Can you see that apostasy is progressive? Joel 1:4 teaches this same truth: “That which the palmerworm hath left hath the locust eaten; and that which the locust hath left hath the cankerworm eaten; and that which the cankerworm hath left hath the caterpillar eaten.” The Hebrew word for palmerworm is gazam. It means “to cut short.” If you take in the spirit of apostasy, your experience will be “cut short.” The Hebrew word for locust is arbeh. It means “to multiply.” The spirit of apostasy wants to multiply its effects and possessors as much as possible.

The word cankerworm, comes from the Hebrew word yelek, which means “to lick or lap.” When apostasy starts to work on others, it is as loving and affectionate as a loyal, loving dog; but this is a deception. The Greek word for caterpillar is chasil. It means “to consume, to eat up.” These four words represent the different stages in the development of the same creature: the locust. But they also depict the progressive, degenerative nature of apostasy.

The word murmurers are found nowhere else in the New Testament. It is derived from the Greek word goggustes. It is used in the Septuagint, the Greek Old Testament, to describe the resentful, discontented grumblings of the children of Israel against Moses as he led them through the wilderness. (See Exodus, Chapters 15 and 17.)

Apostasy has its start in a resentful discontent of God-ordained authority. Seeds of apostasy are sown when an individual resents another person being in a position or making a move that he himself would not make or taking a stand that he himself would not take. Resentment is extremely dangerous! It starts out low, quiet, and careful; just a low, insistent muttering that turns into murmuring.

Murmuring may seem petty and insignificant, but the end of it is not. 1 Corinthians 10:10 says, “Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer.” When you are tempted to fall under the power of murmuring, remember that to murmur against God’s ordained authorities is to murmur against God Himself. (See Exodus 16:7-8.)

SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 6
From Murmurers to Complainers

Complainers. The word complainers is an even stronger, bolder word than murmurers. The Greek word for it is mempsimoiros. It means “to blame for one’s allotted fate in life.” A complainer is dissatisfied with his lot and blames others for it. 1Timothy 6:6 says that “godliness with contentment is great gain.” Paul said in Philippians 4:11, “For I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.”

Complainers are people to whom the truth has become chafing and unbearable. The objects of their scorn are the ones who held truth before them–the true ministry. Initially, they muttered indistinctly, with just a few insinuations here and there. Then, as the truth became more unbearable to them, they became more brazen. They became complainers. People in this condition make God angry! Numbers 11:1 confirms this: “And when the people complained, it displeased the LORD: and the LORD heard it; and his anger was kindled and the fire of the LORD burnt among them, and consumed them that were in the uttermost parts of the camp.”
Unsubmissive, Arrogant Lives

Walking after their own lusts . . . their mouth speaketh great swelling words. Apostates do not just murmur and complain against divine authority–they do not submit their lives to it either. The Amplified Bible says, “These are inveterate murmurers (grumblers) who complain [of their lot in life], going after their own desires [controlled by their passions] . . . .” When this spirit takes over, ones lose control. They operate purely under the flesh. Self restraint is abandoned and replaced with self-will.

The Amplified Bible also says, “Their talk is boastful and arrogant.” Ones who have thrown off the governor of godly restraint speak boastfully and arrogantly in ways they never would have considered while they were under the control of the Holy Spirit. 2 Peter 2:18 says, “They speak great swelling words of vanity.” One translation reads, “They utter arrogant nonsense.” Another translation says they use “phrases that have no meaning.”
Beware of Flattery!

Having men’s persons in admiration because of advantage. What does this mean? It simply means that, as another translation says, “They flatter men for the sake of what they can get from them.” They try to win people to their way of thinking. A flattering tongue is like a disguised viper waiting for the precise moment to inject its venom and bring death. Apostates use their tongues in the same way a snake charms its prey. Psalm 5:9 states, “For there is no faithfulness in their mouth; their inward part is very wickedness; their throat is an open sepulcher; they flatter with their tongue.” Proverbs 20:19 says, “Meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.”
JUST A THOUGHT
The best vitamin for a saint is B 1.

Initially, they muttered indistinctly, with just a few insinuations here and there.
Then, as the truth became more unbearable to them, they became more brazen.
They became complainers.
People in this condition make God angry!

Numbers 11:1 confirms this: “And when the people complained, it displeased the LORD: and the LORD heard it; and his anger was kindled and the fire of the LORD burnt among them, and consumed them that were in the uttermost parts of the camp.”
Walking after their own lusts . . . their mouth speaketh great swelling words.
Apostates do not just murmur and complain against divine authority–they do not submit their lives to it either.
The Amplified Bible says, “These are inveterate murmurers (grumblers) who complain [of their lot in life], going after their own desires [controlled by their passions] . . . .”
When this spirit takes over, ones lose control.
They operate purely under the flesh.
Self restraint is abandoned and replaced with self-will.
The Amplified Bible also says, “Their talk is boastful and arrogant.”
Ones who have thrown off the governor of godly restraint speak boastfully and arrogantly in ways they never would have considered while they were under the control of the Holy Spirit.
2 Peter 2:18 says, “They speak great swelling words of vanity.”
One translation reads, “They utter arrogant nonsense.”
Another translation says they use “phrases that have no meaning.”
Having men’s persons in admiration because of advantage.
What does this mean?
It simply means that, as another translation says, “They flatter men for the sake of what they can get from them.”
They try to win people to their way of thinking.
A flattering tongue is like a disguised viper waiting for the precise moment to inject its venom and bring death.
Apostates use their tongues in the same way a snake charms its prey.
Psalm 5:9 states, “For there is no faithfulness in their mouth; their inward part is very wickedness; their throat is an open sepulcher; they flatter with their tongue.”
Proverbs 20:19 says, “Meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.”

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 7
REMEMBER THE WORD!
Scripture Text: Jude 17

In verses 4 through 16, Jude poured forth stern, sober warnings with a sharp denunciation of those who became involved in apostasy. In verse 17, once more his mind turned to the saints. He began another admonition to them with the term of endearment: beloved.
MEMORY VERSE: Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee (Psalm 119:11).
Which One Are You?

But, beloved. Basically, there are three kinds of people found in the Gospel: saints, sinners, and apostates (see 1 Peter 4:18). Throughout Jude we are dealing with apostates, the “enemies of the cross of Christ” (Philippians 3:18). God has always had a faithful people–the beloved. In the dark age of the Gospel Day, though the saints were secluded in catacombs and caves, Jesus said to them, “To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna” (Revelation 2:17).

As it was stated, in the darkest hours the church has ever faced, there have always been overcomers. In our struggle against apostasy though, it is very easy to feel that we are standing alone while everyone else is being swept away by its deception. That is not so! In Revelation 7:9, John saw “a great multitude [of saints], which no man could number.”

Jesus said in Matthew 12:30, “He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathereth not with me scattereth abroad.” The Apostle Paul wrote in 2 Corinthians 2:16, “To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life.” Individually, the kind of people we are is determined by our responses to the message of the Word. Jesus said those who believed would be saved, but those who would not believe would be “damned” (Mark 16:16).
Take Heed to God’s Word

Remember ye. We will never be moved away by deceptive spirits or evil men if we continue to give the Word of God its proper place in our lives. Psalm 119:9 asks, “Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? By taking heed thereto according to thy word,” John 15:3 states, “Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.”

We are begotten by the Word, and we remain clean by “the washing of water by the word” (Ephesians 5:26). As long as we give heed to the Word, we can remain victorious and be part of the “beloved.” Individuals who have erred may also recover themselves from spiritual error if they will acknowledge the truth of the Word they have heard (see 2 Timothy 2:25-26). This is why Jude said remember ye the words.
Doctrine of Verbal Inspiration

Words which were spoken before of the apostles. The clear indication of Jude’s words is that the words . . . spoken before of the apostles were prophetic and true, inspired by God. This truth is denied, denounced, and derided because those who do not have the Spirit of God cannot fathom the verbal inspiration of the Scriptures. Proverbs 30:5 states, “Every word of God is pure.”
The injunction to not add to (or take away from) God’s Word is recorded throughout the Bible (see Deuteronomy 4:2, Proverbs 30:6, and Revelation 22:19). Why is this injunction so vital? Because “all

LESSON 7

scripture is given by inspiration of God” (2 Timothy 3:16). The Scriptures were written by men who listened to the Holy Spirit. 2 Peter 1:21 tells us that “holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.”

Jude expressly said to remember the words of the Apostles. Every word is vital. When the Apostle Paul spoke of “inspiration,” he used the Greek word theopneustos, which literally means “God breathed.” At man’s creation, when he was yet without natural life, the Lord God “breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul [being]” (Genesis 2:7).

The breath of God also brings spiritual life to man. This is why the enemy and his agents work so against you when you believe in the Bible’s inspiration and accuracy, and apply its teachings to your daily life. Dear saint, do not ever forget that whenever you face an onslaught from the enemy, your victory is in remembering to use the Word. Consider the temptations of Christ. He repeatedly used The Word to rebuke the enemy. Three times in Matthew, Chapter 4, He said, “It is written.”
The Government of Christ

Apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ. This phrase contains several notable truths. The title Lord refers to Christ’s divine position of headship and authority over the church. The name Jesus refers to the mission He came to accomplish in this world (see Matthew 1:21), and Christ means “The Anointed One.” Jesus Christ has a definite government by which He operates the church. Jude, by saying, Remember ye the words which were spoken . . . of the apostles, was validating not only their words and their inspiration but also the offices and officers appointed by Christ to govern the church.

Ephesians 4:11 provides us with a list of the divine offices. They are apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers. How is an individual placed in such an office? First, one must be given the gift (see Ephesians 4:8), then the Lord will set that person in office. The Apostle Paul often let it be known that he was chosen by Christ, “not of men, neither by man” (Galatians 1:1).

God always has a divinely ordered ministry in place–one that is able to see afar off and give us warning from Him. Regardless of what the surrounding conditions may be, as long as God’s people properly regard the Word and the true ministry, they can be victorious in their Christian lives.
JUST A THOUGHT
If others followed your lead, how would they walk?

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 8
MOCKERS IN THE LAST TIME
Scripture Text: Jude 18

This text of Scripture is a continuation of verse 17. In verse 18, Jude has given us an insight to the attitude that apostates hold toward “the words which were spoken before of the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.” They mock the Word! A true indication that one has succumbed to the spirit of apostasy is when he begins to deride the truth and the message of the Word.
MEMORY VERSE: Fools make a mock at sin: but among the righteous there is favor (Proverbs 14:9).
Unity of a True Ministry

How that they told you. This phrase holds a very beautiful truth. In verse 17, Jude revealed to us that when the church holds Christ in His rightful place, as “Lord Jesus Christ,” He will have a divine government in place. There will be ones who are called and “separated unto the gospel of God” (Romans 1:1) to fill divinely ordained offices, and their words will be inspired.

The truth verse 18 reveals is this: when these offices are filled by divinely called individuals, they will operate their gifts under the unction of the Holy Spirit. When they speak, their words will be in harmony with every other one who speaks under divine unction. There are many messengers (“apostles” in verse 17) bearing one message. Isaiah 52:8 states, “Thy watchmen [plural] shall lift up the voice [singular]; with the voice [singular] together shall they [plural] sing: for they shall see eye to eye, when the LORD shall bring again Zion.”

The phrase how that they told you shows the beautiful unity of the morning-time brethren. Paul admonished them to “speak the same thing” and be “perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment” (1 Corinthians 1:10). What a force in this unbelieving world! Unity will convince the world! Read John 17:21-23.
The Mockers and Scoffers

There should be mockers in the last time. The Apostle Peter said in 2 Peter 3:3, “There shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts.” These words are almost identical to what Jude alluded to in our text. Notice, both Jude and Peter spoke of the last time, or “the last days.” Immediately when these words are read, men’s minds begin to think of a time in the future. Jude let the saints of his day (A.D. 66) know that what had been prophesied of as a future occurrence was already a present reality. 1 John 2:18 says, “Little children, it is [present tense] the last time . . . even now are there many antichrists; whereby we know that it is the last time.”

Biblically, the last days began with Pentecost. Acts 2:16-17 states: “But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel; And it shall come to pass in the last days . . . .” That which was spoken of in our text is not something reserved for some time in the future, but rather it was experienced in the apostasy of the first century and has been experienced in every other century whenever these conditions have occurred.

Jude reminded the ones in our text that nothing had occurred that they had not already been warned of. He said that there would be mockers in the last time. This may be startling, but truth should have mockers! It is through the assaults and attacks upon the truth that many individuals are convinced of its authenticity. The centurion who stood beside the Cross saw and heard how ones were reviling Christ. When Jesus cried out and then died, the centurion said, “Truly this man was the Son of God” (Mark 15:39). When a person is being mocked and derided for the sake of the truth, the Spirit of God will use that very persecution to show honest hearts the reality that that one possesses.

SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 8

The word mockers comes from the Greek word empaiktes. The only other place this word is used in the Bible is in 2 Peter 3:3. There it is translated scoffers. This word means “a derider; to jeer at.” Peter used it in reference to those individuals who ask, “Where is the promise of his coming?” (2 Peter 3:4). This tells us that the people who go after their own ungodly desires are blind to spiritual realities. They do not understand that they cannot follow their ungodly desires and follow the Spirit too. Galatians 5:16 says, “Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfill the lust of the flesh.” This is true–and the opposite is true: if you walk after lusts of the flesh, you will not fulfill walking in the Spirit.
Bondage of Ungodly Lusts

Who should walk after their own ungodly lusts. This phrase reveals the sad condition of apostates. Jude said they walk after. The meaning of these words, as they are used here, portrays a beast being led about by a ring in its nose. In verse 10, Jude stated that these men operate “naturally, as brute beasts.” One scholar has said that just as an animal walks obediently behind its master, so do these walk after their own ungodly lusts. Neither the captive bull nor the enslaved apostate has any choice. Both must go wherever they are led. They might claim that they are free; but they are not. They are slaves to their own lusts!
What Are Ungodly Lusts?

Ungodly lusts. The Greek word for lusts is epithumik, which means “a longing, a desire.” These ungodly lusts are not the common kind that bind a sinner. Remember, theses are apostates. 2 Peter 2:18, in the Amplified Bible, states, “For uttering loud boasts of folly, they beguile and lure with lustful desires of the flesh those who are barely escaping from them who are wrongdoers.” The ungodly lusts that dominate apostates keep them constantly working to separate others. They are consumed with an insatiable desire to draw others away from the truth, promising them enlightenment, liberty, and greater truth, but only giving them bondage. This is what is being depicted in 2 Peter 2:18-22.

We should ever be mindful of Jesus’ words: “If the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch” (Matthew 15:14). You should always consider the spiritual condition of individuals who might presume to give you spiritual guidance. If they are following a wrong spirit, you could be affected by their influence. Beware of ones who speak against God’s order in the church, His Spirit, His Word, or His man. Following their ungodly thinking will cause you to become a slave to a spirit of apostasy.
JUST A THOUGHT
“It is better to err on the side of caution than to disregard caution and err.”

LESSON 9
THEY WHO SEPARATE THEMSELVES
Scripture Text: Jude 19
This verse contains the last words that Jude used to describe the condition of apostates. They give a plain and simple summarization of what an apostate does and why.
MEMORY VERSE: Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life (John 6:68).
Promoters of Division

These be they who separate themselves. To understand whom Jude was speaking of in this phrase, look back to verse 18, to the word mockers. The words these and they in verse 19 both refer to this word. Those who have the spirit of mockery and make fun and jeer at the truth, the standard, God’s man, and God’s people are trying to accomplish a purpose through their mocking. They are attempting to embarrass God’s people away from their stand for the truth.

Jude said, These . . . separate themselves. The Greek word that separate comes from is apodiorizo. This word is composed of several portions. Apo means “from,” dio means “asunder,” and horizo means “to limit.” Together, they simply mean those who have put themselves asunder from the limits. One scholar’s translation of this word is, “they who bring about divisions because of borderlines, or limits.” Martin Luther interpreted it as “those who make factions.”

The “limits” are boundaries that God has set in His Word for the control of our humanity and conduct. Men who have yielded themselves to the spirit of apostasy scoff and mock at the law of God. They deny the authority of the Scriptures and refuse to submit to its dictates. Spiritually, they are outside the body of Christ, even though they continue to profess and try to allure others to their way of thinking. To induce, promote, or further division is SIN!

Galatians 5:19-21 lists the works of the flesh. Verse 21 declares, “They which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.” Verse 20 mentions “heresies,” which in the Greek language is interpreted sects, or parties. In 1 Corinthians 1:10 and 1 Corinthians 12:25, Paul earnestly told the Corinthians that they should have no divisions among them. 1 Corinthians 1:13 asks the question, “Is Christ divided?” The obvious answer is “No.”

The clear inference is that His body should not be divided either. However, there are men who separate themselves. Sad as it is, this act of separation is a revealing work. 1 John 2:19 says, “They went out from us, but they were not of us [how do we know?]: for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us.” 1 Corinthians 11:19 states, “For there must be also heresies [sects] among you [why?], that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.” Heresy and division help to reveal those who really are holding to the truth and are in the family of God.
A Sensual Manner

Sensual. What does this word mean? The Greek word that it comes from is used six times in the New Testament. It is translated twice as sensual: here, in our text, and in James 3:15. (In James it is used to show a change in one’s thinking from “earthly” to “devilish.”)

The Greek word that sensual is derived from is psychikos (a form of the word psyche, which refers to the soul). The word psychikos refers to man in his earthly nature, but it goes deeper and also reveals why he is under the power of that nature. This lets us know that the condition of men’s souls, this sensual condition, is what

causes apostates to behave in such a way that they will work to “subvert whole houses” (Titus 1:11). Now what causes this sensual condition?
The Religious Spirits

Having not the Spirit. If there is any question as to whether apostates may perhaps be merely misguided believers, this phrase lays that question to rest. Romans 8:9 plainly says, “Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.” Man is a three-part being consisting of “spirit and soul and body” (1 Thessalonians 5:23). He is first a soul. He has a body, and he possesses a spirit. Man is what he is and does what he does because of the spirit he possesses. The ones in our text are referred to as having not the Spirit. Why should we notice this? (There were multitudes of people who did not have the Spirit.) We should notice this because the “mockers” claimed to be part of God’s church!

Apostates still say they are part of the church, but the Spirit has taken His departure from their lives. They became “empty” and thus a prey for religious spirits. Matthew 12:44-45 says that when “. . . he findeth it [a spiritual house] empty, swept, and garnished. Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself and they enter in and dwell there.”

Prophetically, the seven spirits are the religious spirits that motivate the “seven women” in Isaiah 4:1. They are the religious spirits that the church has faced in the seven periods of the Gospel Day. The spirit we are facing today is the ecumenical spirit that is portrayed in Revelation, Chapter 17. The people overcome by this spirit think everyone has some good points and is right. They readily fellowship everyone; that is, everyone except the ones in the truth. They feel those people are too judgmental.

What is the lesson? Ones having not the Spirit, do have a spirit–a religious spirit. These are not merely misguided men who have “the spirit of the world” (1 Corinthians 2:12). These people have become possessed with the spirit of apostasy that promotes division and the rise of religious groups not based in the truth. Though these individuals consider themselves to be very spiritual, Jude has proclaimed the truth–they do not even have the Spirit!
Grieve Not the Spirit

The importance of the Spirit cannot be stressed enough! It is the Spirit that convicts (John 16:8). It is the Spirit that God uses to give spiritual life (Romans 8:10). The Spirit guides us and empowers us to be witnesses (John 16:13 and Acts 1:8). The Spirit brings us spiritual understanding (Ephesians 1:18). Seven times in Revelation, Chapters 2 and 3, Jesus said, “He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith.”

In this period of the Gospel Day, when unclean spirits have “come out” (Revelation 16:13) and gone into the whole world, it would be best for each of us to do as Malachi 2:16 admonishes: “take heed to your spirit.” Make certain that you do not grieve, or hurt, the Holy Spirit (Ephesians 4:30). If you do, He may take His departure from your life, leaving you defenseless against a religious spirit. Cherish the presence of the Holy Spirit and do all that He bids you to do. The ones in our text did not do that, and they ended up separating themselves.
JUST A THOUGHT
If you are feeling the effects of truth decay, try brushing up on your Bible reading.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 10
THE CALL TO ACTION–PART 1
Scripture Text: Jude 20

Abraham told the rich man in Luke 16:26, “Between us and you there is a great gulf fixed.” There is always a gulf between the righteous and the unrighteous. This gulf is clearly depicted in the contrast of verses 18-19 to verse 20. Verse 18 speaks of “mockers” and “ungodly lusts.” Verse 19 refers to the apostates as “sensual, having not the Spirit.” Verse 20 mentions building up yourselves, holy faith, and praying in the Holy Ghost. What a difference in interests, attributes, and characters!

MEMORY VERSE: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye steadfast, unmovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord. (1 Corinthians 15:58).
Exercising Your Experience

But ye, beloved, building up. From verse 20, throughout the balance of his letter, Jude admonished the beloved. In verse 20, he used two action words to portray what the saints must continually be doing to remain victorious in the face of apostasy: building and praying. Maintaining a victorious experience in the midst of a swirling sea of apostasy requires a high level of activity and effort on our part. Jesus said, “Strive to enter in at the strait gate” (Luke 13:24).

The Greek word for strive is agonizomai (our English word agony is derived from it). It is the same Greek word used in John 18:36. There it is translated as “fight.” It is also used in Colossians 4:12 and is translated as “laboring fervently.” 1 Peter 4:18 states, “And if the righteous scarcely [the Greek word here is molis, which means „toil, much work, much difficulty‟] be saved . . . .” Each of these words represents action and effort.

The words building up are in direct opposition to the words used in the previous verses. There Jude spoke of ones who were endeavoring to tear down the work of God. However, Nehemiah 4:17 tells us that when God‟s people were working to rebuild the wall, “everyone with one of his hands wrought in the work, and with the other hand held a weapon.” This Scripture helps us to understand what we must do to “fight the good fight of faith” (1 Timothy 6:12). The admonition, to be building up, is a call to take the trowel in hand while not allowing the enemies of truth to hinder the work of God.
No Time to Quit

Building up yourselves. There are many truths portrayed in the word building. The act of building infers a present, continued, and life-long task. The Apostle Paul said in Philippians 3:12-13: “Not as though I had already attained . . . . Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended.” This is where all who have fallen under the spirit of apostasy have erred: they accepted the thought that they had arrived, so to speak. 1 Corinthians 10:12 gives us this warning: “Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.”

The thought of building, as something we continually need to be doing, reveals to us that what we have done today is not sufficient to carry us through all the way. The foolish virgins made this error. Matthew 25:3 states, “They that were foolish took their lamps [what they had presently], and took no oil with them [or made no provision for the future].” They thought what they had then was enough to carry them all the way. What a fatal error!

There is no place for us to settle down and become complacent. Jude said to be building up yourselves. That means we must be active participants in our own salvation. God will do what men cannot, but He will not do what men can. Philippians 2:12 says to “work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.” God will work it in us, but it is up to us to work it out. He will enlighten us and provide us grace, but we must do the “work.” 2 Corinthians 7:1 tells us to “cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit.”

SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 10
Adding to Your Faith

On your most holy faith. Our faith is the basis of our experience, but it is not the end of it. In the Emphatic Diaglott, Hebrews 11:1 says, “But Faith is a Basis.” A “basis” is not an end result but rather a foundation upon which one can build. Webster’s New World Dictionary says it is “the base, foundation, or chief supporting factor of anything.” 2 Peter 1:5-7 says: “Add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge; and to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity.”

In the thought of building . . . on your most holy faith, Jude was saying that those who have fallen prey to apostasy have done so because they first allowed their individual experiences to stagnate. If you want to be immune from the infection of apostasy, you must keep exercising your experience. “Exercise thyself rather unto godliness” (1 Timothy 4:7). Do not let your experience become stagnant. It is in stagnant water that frogs make their homes. Religious “unclean spirits like frogs” (Revelation 16:13) will try to move in on you if your experience becomes as a stagnant pool.
Praying in the Spirit

Praying in the Holy Ghost. In this last phrase in verse 20, Jude issued another call to action. Several truths are in this phrase: the first one is that genuine prayer is an insulation against apostasy. Many dear souls would never have made the moves they made had they really prayed and listened to the Holy Spirit. The second truth is that we ought to pray from the heart, not merely say or recite prayers as much of religion does.

The third truth is that real praying must incorporate the Holy Ghost. He must be involved if our praying is to really constitute prayer. Real praying is not just speaking our minds but yielding to the leadership of the Spirit. There is always a gulf between the righteous and the unrighteous.
This gulf is clearly depicted in the contrast of verses 18-19 to verse 20.
Verse 18 speaks of “mockers” and “ungodly lusts.”
Verse 19 refers to the apostates as “sensual, having not the Spirit.”
Verse 20 mentions building up yourselves, holy faith, and praying in the Holy Ghost.
What a difference in interests, attributes, and characters!
But ye, beloved, building up.
From verse 20, throughout the balance of his letter, Jude admonished the beloved.
In verse 20, he used two action words to portray what the saints must continually be doing to remain victorious in the face of apostasy: building and praying.
Maintaining a victorious experience in the midst of a swirling sea of apostasy requires a high level of activity and effort on our part.
Jesus said, “Strive to enter in at the strait gate” (Luke 13:24).
The Greek word for strive is agonizomai (our English word agony is derived from it).
It is the same Greek word used in John 18:36.
There it is translated as “fight.”
It is also used in Colossians 4:12 and is translated as “laboring fervently.”
1 Peter 4:18 states, “And if the righteous scarcely [the Greek word here is molis, which means „toil, much work, much difficulty‟] be saved . . . .”
Each of these words represents action and effort.
The words building up are in direct opposition to the words used in the previous verses.
There Jude spoke of ones who were endeavoring to tear down the work of God.
However, Nehemiah 4:17 tells us that when God‟s people were working to rebuild the wall, “everyone with one of his hands wrought in the work, and with the other hand held a weapon.”
This Scripture helps us to understand what we must do to “fight the good fight of faith” (1 Timothy 6:12).
The admonition, to be building up, is a call to take the trowel in hand while not allowing the enemies of truth to hinder the work of God.
Building up yourselves.
There are many truths portrayed in the word building.
The act of building infers a present, continued, and life-long task.
The Apostle Paul said in Philippians 3:12-13: “Not as though I had already attained . . . .
Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended.”
This is where all who have fallen under the spirit of apostasy have erred: they accepted the thought that they had arrived, so to speak.
1 Corinthians 10:12 gives us this warning: “Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.”
The thought of building, as something we continually need to be doing, reveals to us that what we have done today is not sufficient to carry us through all the way.
The foolish virgins made this error.
Matthew 25:3 states, “They that were foolish took their lamps [what they had presently], and took no oil with them [or made no provision for the future].”
They thought what they had then was enough to carry them all the way.
What a fatal error!
There is no place for us to settle down and become complacent.
Jude said to be building up yourselves.
That means we must be active participants in our own salvation.
God will do what men cannot, but He will not do what men can.
Philippians 2:12 says to “work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.”
God will work it in us, but it is up to us to work it out.
He will enlighten us and provide us grace, but we must do the “work.”
2 Corinthians 7:1 tells us to “cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit.”
On your most holy faith.
Our faith is the basis of our experience, but it is not the end of it.
In the Emphatic Diaglott, Hebrews 11:1 says, “But Faith is a Basis.”
A “basis” is not an end result but rather a foundation upon which one can build.
Webster’s New World Dictionary says it is “the base, foundation, or chief supporting factor of anything.”

2 Peter 1:5-7 says: “Add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge; and to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity.”

Do not let your experience become stagnant.
It is in stagnant water that frogs make their homes.
Religious “unclean spirits like frogs” (Revelation 16:13) will try to move in on you if your experience becomes as a stagnant pool.
Praying in the Holy Ghost.
In this last phrase in verse 20, Jude issued another call to action.
Several truths are in this phrase: the first one is that genuine prayer is an insulation against apostasy.
Many dear souls would never have made the moves they made had they really prayed and listened to the Holy Spirit.
The second truth is that we ought to pray from the heart, not merely say or recite prayers as much of religion does.
The third truth is that real praying must incorporate the Holy Ghost.
He must be involved if our praying is to really constitute prayer.
Real praying is not just speaking our minds but yielding to the leadership of the Spirit.
Romans 8:26 tells us that “we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us.”
Real prayer brings the flesh into subjection and allows the Holy Spirit to commune with God.
Romans 8:27 tells us, “And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.”
Praying in the Holy Ghost allows Him to direct the praying.
The fourth truth is this: we should not only speak but listen.
Praying in the Holy Ghost not only allows us to speak to God, it also allows Him to speak to us.
The reason that many people have made and are making poor decisions concerning apostasy is that when they are done speaking to God, they get up and leave.
To receive divine guidance and direction that will keep us from being moved by the spirits of the day, we should take time to reflect and repose, allowing the Holy Spirit to commune with us.
When you pray, do you stay until you hear what He has to say?

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 11
THE CALL TO ACTION–PART 2
Scripture Text: Jude 21

Verse 21 is the continuation of thoughts that were begun in verse 20. The words in verse 21 serve as a call to action to the army of the Lord. “The weapons of our warfare are not carnal” (2 Corinthians 10:4). They are of a spiritual nature. This is why we were told to be “building” and “praying” (verse 20); then in verse 21, to “keep” and be “looking.” The truth will always have foes. We cannot allow ourselves to become so involved with thoughts of them that we forget the supreme purpose for which we (the church) are in this world.
MEMORY VERSE: But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us, Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ. Ephesians 2:4-5
A Personal Responsibility

Keep yourselves. This appeal is a personal one. Regardless of what groups of men may do or what moves or choices your family may make, you are individually responsible for your own soul. On that great day, we shall stand as individuals, not as families or as groups. 2 Corinthians 5:10 plainly says, “For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body.”

The phrase keep yourselves lets us know that we cannot govern others. The opposite is true as well: no one else can do this for us–not good parents, not excellent youth leaders, not burdened Sunday school teachers–not even a godly pastor can do this for us. The exhortation Jude gave the saints when he used the word keep was that an active, constant effort should be maintained on their part.
Remaining in God’s Love

In the love of God. In Luke 15:11-32, the prodigal son started his life enjoying the presence of his father. He had all the benefits of sonship. He could enjoy his father’s presence and experience his love. One day he chose to remove himself from his father’s house, from his father’s presence, and from all the benefits of being with his father. He put himself in a position where he could not enjoy his father’s love, even though his father, deeply wounded, still loved him. The son had moved himself to such a far-off position that the love of the father was of no benefit to him. It is possible to engage in such sinful activity that you move from God’s love to His hate.

In the Word of God, there are six things the Lord hates. One is found in Proverbs 6:19: “He that soweth discord among brethren.” One of the preventatives for apostasy is staying in the love of God. We must ever work at keeping ourselves in the love of God. There are many misconceptions concerning God’s love. It is not a feeling or an emotion. The word love is derived from the Greek word agape. It means a commitment to action. (If a man truly loves his wife, there are certain things that he does and certain things that he does not do.)

John 15:9 states, “As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you: continue ye in my love.” How do we do that? John 15:10 tells us, “If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love.” 1 John 5:3 says, “For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.” The only way to not be one of those who “kept not their first estate” is to keep God’s commandments. James 2:10 states, “For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.” Full obedience is the only safe position to occupy.
Looking for God’s Mercy

SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 11

Looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ. The word looking is the culmination of the other three elements that Jude admonished us to have working in our lives. If you are “building” on your personal experience, “praying” as you ought, and keeping yourself “in the love of God,” then you will have a missionary eye. John 4:35 says, “Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? Behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.”

We are to be looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ. What does this mean? Watch for opportunities to show the mercy of God to the lost. Have an eye that is quick to spot those who may respond to an offer of mercy. Too many times, when we are involved in a battle against apostasy, we become so engrossed with the battle that we see nothing else. We need to remember our mission, which is to introduce souls to the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Having Eternal Life

Unto eternal life. These last words of our text reveal two truths. The first one is, when we lead men and women to “the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ,” we are leading them unto eternal life. Eternal life is not some distant promise that we will receive after we die, but it begins here and now: when we receive an experience of salvation. John 3:36 declares, “He that believeth [present tense] on the Son hath [present tense] everlasting life.” 1 John 5:11 tells us, “And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.” When Christ, through the Holy Spirit, makes His advent into one’s life, eternal life comes as well.

The second truth found in the phrase unto eternal life is that every (true) child of God is endeavoring to stay in the love of God and is living with eternity in view. If you will do the things necessary to have a healthy experience and gauge everything by eternity’s standard, you will never be swept away by storms of apostasy. The sum thought of all of this is that if we do as we ought, we will come out as we ought. “Surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God” (Ecclesiastes 8:12).
JUST A THOUGHT
If, during our lifetime, we live with thoughts of eternity; then, during eternity, we will not regret the thoughts of our lifetime.

paragraphs.text: In the love of God. In Luke 15:11-32, the prodigal son started his life enjoying the presence of his father. He had all the benefits of sonship. He could enjoy his father’s presence and experience his love. One day he chose to remove himself from his father’s house, from his father’s presence, and from all the benefits of being with his father. He put himself in a position where he could not enjoy his father’s love, even though his father, deeply wounded, still loved him. The son had moved himself to such a far-off position that the love of the father was of no benefit to him. It is possible to engage in such sinful activity that you move from God’s love to His hate.
